text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any immediate deformity or inability to bend the tip of the finger after the injury, and is there any significant bruising or discoloration present? I need to determine if this is a simple sprain, a fracture, or a tendon injury like a mallet finger.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the mechanism of injury and the specific inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint, this presentation is highly suggestive of a flexor digitorum profundus avulsion, commonly known as a Jersey finger. I will order an imaging study to confirm the diagnosis and assess for any bony fragment avulsion. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_hand
